readMeFirst: data/r2-regate.json records the repair loop re-measured with compiler/eval/spike's gate in front of it, and names the two LTO probes as the thing it does NOT cover: they are gated the same way, they write no tracked rows, and so there was nothing in data/ of theirs to compare against. This file closes that, differently: the probes still write no tracked rows, so what is compared is the numbers their own prose quotes in tools/LTO.md against the numbers a gated run produces. The comparison is by hand and transcribed here; test/lto-regate.test.mjs reads the numbers back OUT of LTO.md and holds this record to them, so a transcription error or a later edit of LTO.md fails a test.
question: do the numbers tools/LTO.md quotes for the two LTO probes reproduce with the spike/recovery gate in front of the run?
whyItWasOpen: The gate was wired into both probes on 2026-09-12 (lto-probe.mjs:278, lto-probe-gcc.mjs:312). LTO.md's last content change was earlier the same day, so every number in it was taken before the gate existed -- the code was gated and the prose was not, the same split r2-regate.json records for the rows. LTO.md does not contain the word gate.

toolchain.ld: GNU ld (GNU Binutils for Ubuntu) 2.42, through the driver and gcc's LTO linker plugin

scope.whyOneLevel: -O2 is the level at which both probes' default run is defined, the level LTO.md's clang Run E and gcc Run A rows both cover, and the one configuration at which the spike gate has a discriminating pair registered for each vendor (`--opts -O0` alone has no such pair and the probes refuse the run). The other levels LTO.md quotes (-O1, -O3, -Os, and the --all-removable runs) were NOT re-measured here.
scope.forms: clang: full and thin. gcc: the one form gcc has.

runs.comparedAgainst: LTO.md Run E (full and thin, -O2, 113 files)
LTO.md Run E (full and thin, -O2, 113 files)
LTO.md gcc Run A, -O2 row (108 files)
LTO.md gcc Run A, -O2 row (108 files)

whyTwoPluginsPerVendor: The first run of each vendor used the plugin this branch's build directory holds, which is a REBUILD of the same source and has a different sha256 from the one LTO.md quotes. Reproducing a number with the gate added AND the binary changed does not separate the two, so each vendor was then run again with the exact binary the prose quotes -- found in the lab, digest verified -- and that run is the one the claim rests on. The rebuild is kept here because it is evidence of something else: the figures do not depend on the particular binary.
notMeasuredHere: Every level except -O2. LTO.md quotes -O1 (62 of 113 for clang), -O3 and -Os, clang run F (--all-removable, 133 files) and gcc run B (--all-removable, 133 files). None of those was re-run under the gate, so for those rows the original statement still stands: they are pre-gate lab output.
The clang probe's --sample path, and both probes' --plan and --files selections.
Anything about a second machine. These are four runs on one WSL host; LTO.md's own figures were taken on the same one, so agreement between them is not independent replication.

provenance.numbers: transcribed by hand from the four run logs -- the probes refuse --write-data (exit 4), so no tool wrote this file. test/lto-regate.test.mjs re-reads the corresponding numbers out of tools/LTO.md and compares them to the values here, which catches a transcription error in one direction and an edit of LTO.md in the other.
provenance.gate: lab-run -- read from the first line of each log (`spike gate: ESTABLISHED ... injection RED (as required) ... discriminating`); nothing here recomputes it
provenance.wallClockSeconds: lab-run -- from `time`, two of the four runs sharing the machine with the other two, and expected to differ elsewhere
